summary:
This is the **first page of the index** (printed page 609, PDF 633). It opens with the large *index* title and covers the letter **A**, from *abstraction acquisition* to *axis_names argument*.

**How to use it.** Index entries cite **printed** page numbers. To find the page in this PDF companion, **add 24** (for example, printed 464 becomes PDF 488). Indented lines are sub-entries of the heading above them, and a range such as 576–584 means a continuous discussion.

**What clusters here.**
- **AI and AGI, the big picture.** *AI (artificial intelligence)* 2 (PDF 26) has many sub-entries: AI winters 14 (PDF 38), building intelligence 576–584 (PDF 600–608), local vs. extreme generalization 573 (PDF 597), search and symbols 584–594 (PDF 608–618), and future developments 606 (PDF 630). Related entries are *AGI* 13, 571, 594 (PDF 37, 595, 618), *ARC-AGI* 581, 583 (PDF 605, 607), *ARC Prize* 581, *abstraction acquisition* 578 (PDF 602), *automatons* 571 and *AI summer* 597.
- **Attention.** *attention* 464 (PDF 488), with *dot-product attention* 439 (PDF 463) and *Transformer architecture* 437 (PDF 461). *attention_mask* is at 446–447 (PDF 470–471).
- **Optimizers.** *adam optimizer* 247, 379, 490 (PDF 271, 403, 514) and *AdamW optimizer* 529 (PDF 553).
- **Models and techniques.** *autoencoders* 510 (PDF 534), *autoregressive model* 426 (PDF 450), *activation functions* 109 (PDF 133), *adversarial examples* 567 (PDF 591), *anomaly detection* 352 (PDF 376), *augmenting text data* 413.
- **Keras API names.** *adapt()* 399, *add()* 192, *append()* 192, *axis_names argument* 553 (distribution API).

concepts.name: attention (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 464 (PDF 488), with sub-entries for dot-product attention at 439 (PDF 463) and the Transformer architecture at 437 (PDF 461).
concepts.intuition: If you are looking for where the book builds attention step by step, start at the Transformer chapter around PDF 461–471.
concepts.technical: Related index entries: attention_mask 446, 447 (PDF 470–471) and attention mechanisms 462 (PDF 486).
concepts.significance: Attention is the core mechanism behind the Transformers and LLMs covered in the later chapters.
concepts.example: To read about dot-product attention, go to PDF 463 (printed 439).
concepts.misconception: The page numbers on this index page are not PDF pages. Add 24 to each one.

concepts.name: Adam / AdamW optimizer (index entries)
concepts.definition: adam optimizer is indexed at printed 247, 379, 490 (PDF 271, 403, 514). AdamW optimizer is at 529 (PDF 553).
concepts.intuition: These are the places where Adam is used in practical examples. The page shows nothing more than the page numbers.
concepts.technical: Each locator points to a code example that uses the optimizer in compile(), not to a derivation of the algorithm.
concepts.significance: Adam is the default optimizer in most of the book's later examples.
concepts.example: PDF 553 (printed 529) uses AdamW in the image-generation chapter.
concepts.misconception: The index does not explain how Adam works; it only tells you where it appears.

concepts.name: AGI / ARC-AGI (index entries)
concepts.definition: AGI (artificial general intelligence) is at printed 13, 571, 594 (PDF 37, 595, 618). ARC-AGI is at 581, 583 (PDF 605, 607).
concepts.intuition: These entries lead to the authors' views on the limits of current AI and on how to measure real intelligence.
concepts.technical: Related sub-entries under AI: building intelligence 576–584 and search and symbols 584–594.
concepts.significance: They lead into chapter 19's argument that generalization power, not scale, is what defines intelligence.
concepts.example: Go to PDF 605 (printed 581) for the ARC Prize.
concepts.misconception: ARC-AGI is a benchmark, not a model.
